messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Multicollinearity in unmarked
parts:
The link that Ken gives is definitely useful for get measures of multicollinearity.  But to state what maybe isn't always obvious:  there is really no such thing as "accounting for" or "controlling for" multicollinearity with the same data set.  For example is distance to water is highly correlated with elevation, then one can't drop one of those variables and then claim causal inferences about the variable that remains in the model.  Removing variables that are correlated can certainly result in fewer models being examined without much loss of predictive ability and produce more numerically stable models.

So knowing the level and where multicollinearity exists in the data is a good thing to know.  It's just that with the same data set unambiguous inferences about certain coefficients aren't possible if variables are tossed out based on tests of multicollinearity.

My apologies if I've just stated the obvious.

Jim

Hi Caroline, 
VIF is supported in unmarked - use the vif function you need to specify the model and type (state/detect) that you want to examine
vif(mod, type)
Hope that helps!
